examples.en: I shave in front of the mirror every morning.
Yesterday I had no time, so I shaved in a rush.

examples.ko: 내일 면접이 있어서 일찍 면도할 거예요.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'll shave early.
My face stung while I was shaving.
I shaved and then put on lotion.
You look clean-faced because you shaved.

explain: '면도기', '면도날', '면도크림'처럼 도구 이름에도 '면도'가 들어가요. 수염과 얼굴 털을 밀 때 쓰고, 머리카락을 짧게 자를 때는 '자르다', '깎다'를 써요.
explain_en: The word 면도 also appears in tool names like 면도기, 면도날, and 면도크림. It is used for shaving a beard or facial hair, while cutting hair short uses 자르다 or 깎다.

examples.en: I tried to find constellations in the night sky.
My star sign is Pisces.

examples.ko: 별자리가 잘 보이는 곳으로 캠핑 갔어요.
examples.en: We went camping where the constellations are easy to see.
I checked my horoscope with a friend.
The stories about constellations are fun.
In the old days, people told direction by the constellations.

explain: '무슨 별자리예요?'는 하늘의 별이 아니라 생일로 정해지는 별자리를 묻는 말로 나와요. 운세 이야기를 할 때 많이 물어요.
explain_en: 'Museun byeoljariyeyo?' asks your star sign, which is set by your birthday, not a pattern in the sky. It comes up when people talk about horoscopes.

examples.en: I caught a crucian carp in the pond.
A crucian carp jumped above the water.
This crucian carp is as big as a palm.
The children fed the crucian carp.

examples.ko: 붕어로 만든 찜이 유명한 식당에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a restaurant famous for braised crucian carp.
They sell crucian carp at the market too.

explain: 붕어 모양 간식 '붕어빵'에는 붕어가 들어가지 않아요. 연못이나 강에 사는 민물고기라서 낚시나 매운탕 이야기에도 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 가족끼리 얼굴이 똑같이 닮았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when family members look exactly alike.

explain_en: The fish-shaped snack 붕어빵 contains no 붕어. It is a freshwater fish of ponds and rivers, so it comes up in talk about fishing and 매운탕.

examples.en: Tigers hunt at night.
People in the old days hunted animals with bows.
I saw a lion hunting on television.

examples.ko: 독수리가 토끼를 사냥할 때 정말 빨라요.
examples.en: An eagle is really fast when it hunts a rabbit.
My grandfather hunted in the mountains when he was young.

examples.ko: 이 동물은 무리를 지어 사냥해서 먹이를 구해요.
examples.en: This animal hunts in a group to find food.

explain: 사람도 동물도 먹이를 잡을 때 '사냥하다'를 써요. '사냥을 가다', '사냥을 나가다'처럼 '사냥'과 다른 동사를 같이 써도 돼요. 낚시로 물고기를 잡을 때는 '낚시하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Both people and animals '사냥하다' when they catch prey. You can also use the noun with another verb, as in '사냥을 가다' or '사냥을 나가다'. Catching fish with a rod is '낚시하다'.

examples.en: The file was moved to another folder.
The luggage is moved onto the truck.
The patient is being taken to the hospital.
Let's restart from the new position.

examples.ko: 사진이 다른 곳으로 이동될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: The photos may be moved elsewhere.
The desk has been moved to the window.

explain: 사람이 걸어가는 게 아니라 물건, 자료, 환자처럼 다른 힘으로 옮겨질 때 써요. 내가 직접 가는 건 '이동하다'를 써요. 컴퓨터에서 파일을 옮겼다고 할 때도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used when things like objects, data or a patient are moved by some other force, not when a person walks. When you go by yourself, the active verb is used. It also comes up often for files being moved on a computer.

p.n: 이전되다 is for offices or institutions, so it sounds odd for furniture.

examples.en: We bought a new rice cooker for our newlywed home.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥이 밥이 다 됐다고 알려 줘요.
examples.en: The rice cooker tells me the rice is done.
You can also steam food with a rice cooker.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥에 쌀과 물을 넣고 취사 버튼을 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I put rice and water in the rice cooker and pressed the cook button.
This rice cooker keeps food warm for a long time.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥 뚜껑을 열자 김이 확 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the rice cooker lid, steam rushed up.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '밥솥'이라고 해도 통해요. 버튼은 '취사'(밥 짓기)와 '보온'(따뜻하게 두기)이 기본이에요. 밥을 '짓다'라고 하는 점도 함께 알아 두세요.
explain_en: In daily life, just saying '밥솥' also works. The basic buttons are '취사' (cook) and '보온' (keep warm). Also note that rice is 'made' with the verb '짓다'.

examples.en: I turn left at the next signal.
The car in front suddenly turned left.
If you turn left at that intersection, you will see a bank.
Many cars are turning left, so the road is jammed.

examples.ko: 길을 잘못 들어서 좌회전할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I took a wrong road and could not turn left.
Turn left and go just two blocks, and you will arrive.

explain: 반대말은 '우회전하다'예요. 좌회전은 주로 차를 몰 때 써요. 걸어서 길을 알려 줄 때는 '왼쪽으로 가세요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Its opposite is 우회전하다. It is mainly for driving. When giving walking directions, 왼쪽으로 가세요 sounds more natural.

examples.en: There is a small globe on the desk.

examples.ko: 지구본을 돌리면서 가고 싶은 나라를 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I spun the globe and looked for countries I want to visit.
I bought a globe as a birthday present for my child.

examples.ko: 지구본으로 보면 한국과 브라질이 얼마나 먼지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: On a globe you can see how far apart Korea and Brazil are.

examples.ko: 지구본은 세계 지도보다 실제 모양에 더 가까워요.
examples.en: A globe is closer to the real shape than a world map.
Shall we try finding our country on this globe?

explain: 평평한 '세계 지도'와 달리 둥근 모양이라 나라의 크기와 거리를 더 실제에 가깝게 볼 수 있어요. 보통 '지구본을 돌리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike a flat '세계 지도' (world map), the round shape shows country sizes and distances closer to reality. The usual collocation is '지구본을 돌리다' (to spin the globe).
